rule_description: Containers add no Linux capabilities beyond the Pod Security baseline set
Pods do not share the host network, PID or IPC namespace
Pods mount no hostPath volumes
Containers bind no host ports
Windows pods do not run as HostProcess containers
Containers do not run privileged
Containers keep the default /proc mask
Containers set no custom SELinux user or role and only permitted types
AppArmor profiles are runtime default or localhost only
evidence_note: Checks the AppArmor annotation only. The securityContext.appArmorProfile field (Kubernetes 1.30 and later) is not checked, so a pod can set an unconfined profile there and still pass; CM-6 evidence does not cover that field.

rule_description: Seccomp profiles are runtime default or localhost only
Pods set only the safe sysctls
Containers drop ALL capabilities and add at most NET_BIND_SERVICE
Containers set allowPrivilegeEscalation to false
Containers run with a non-zero user id
Containers set runAsNonRoot to true
Seccomp profiles are set and are runtime default or localhost
Pods use only the volume types the restricted profile allows
Roles and ClusterRoles grant no wildcard verbs
Nothing is bound to system:anonymous or system:unauthenticated or system:masters
Pods do not mount a service-account token unless they declare it
cluster-admin is bound only to the group itsp:daw-admins
evidence_note: Evidences that only the designated administrator group holds cluster-admin. It cannot show where that group's identities connect from; the dedicated administration workstation itself (SI-400) needs configuration review.

rule_description: Containers declare CPU and memory requests and a memory limit
Workloads are kept out of the default namespace
Images carry an explicit tag other than latest
evidence_note: Supporting evidence only: an image tagged latest leaves the baseline configuration undefined, but pinned tags alone do not make a baseline.
